concept: MongoDB for VS Code: connections, playgrounds and the Copilot participant

claims.text: The documented connection choices are a connection string, an advanced-settings form that builds a connection string, and existing Atlas CLI configurations. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Atlas connection troubleshooting distinguishes credential problems from DNS problems: check username, password, target cluster and authSource for authentication failures; an ISP DNS server that lacks SRV lookup support can cause DNSHostNotFound. (low confidence)
The legacy `/query` workflow supplies the relevant collection schema to GitHub Copilot and asks the user to choose a collection when the prompt omits one. (low confidence)

The historical /query workflow supplies relevant collection schema to Copilot, asks the user to select a collection when none is specified, and lets the user open generated queries in a playground or run them directly. (low confidence)
Playground execution displays results in a Playground Results pane, or in a new tab if split view is disabled. (medium confidence)

The historical investigation VSCODE-432 reports millions of Playground Loaded events per day and says the team temporarily disabled the Segment source and event tracking while seeking a cause; it does not establish a present-day event rate or root cause. (low confidence)
The documented `mdb.defaultLimit` default is `10` documents when browsing a collection. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Use `require()` to reuse local JavaScript code or load native and external Node modules in playgrounds. MongoDB documents a local validation helper exported with `module.exports` and imported by file path. (medium confidence)
Use the Command Palette command MongoDB: Create MongoDB Playground to open a playground with sample commands. (medium confidence)

For command-line script execution, mongosh documents `--file` or `-f` and recommends always using these flags when passing filenames because bare filenames can fail with other arguments. (medium confidence)
MongoDB for VS Code supports Atlas and self-managed deployments, including standalone, replica set, and sharded cluster hosts. (medium confidence)

In Atlas, open the cluster Connect dialog and select MongoDB for VS Code to obtain the connection instructions; the Atlas documentation then directs users to connect with that connection string in the extension. (low confidence)

For replica sets, the extension recommends a replica set SRV record or Replica Set Name instead of a direct member connection: a member role change can close the connection or leave stale data. Direct connections to analytics nodes are unsupported. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

In GitHub issue 1333, the reporter describes querySrv ECONNREFUSED with VS Code 1.132.0 and MongoDB Extension 1.16.1 on Windows while the same Atlas SRV string works in Compass. This is an attributed failure report, not a verified root cause or proof that all Atlas connections fail. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-07)

The extension documents encrypted storage of connection strings and credentials through the VS Code API. Microsoft describes its SecretStorage API as encrypted, platform-dependent storage whose secrets do not sync across machines. (medium confidence)

Disconnecting closes the active connection and requires reconnection before further data interaction. Removing a saved connection removes it from both the current workspace and VS Code globally. (low confidence)
The legacy MongoDB Copilot participant generated MongoDB queries from natural language inside VS Code; Microsoft and a separate developer blog both described that integration. (high confidence)

MongoDB issue VSCODE-791 reports the literal `Copilot model not found` error for the participant, lists affected version 1.16.1, and records fix version 1.17.0; this is tracker metadata rather than an independently tested repair. (low confidence)

MongoDB Playgrounds provide a JavaScript environment in VS Code for prototyping queries, aggregations, CRUD operations, and MongoDB commands. Saved playgrounds can document database interactions alongside application code. (medium confidence)

Playground logging and query results use different destinations: console messages appear in the VS Code Output panel, while Playground Results appear in an editor pane or tab. An output troubleshooting thread reports confusion between these destinations. (medium confidence)

A November 2021 issue report says extension v0.6.10 returned `[COMMON-90002] load is not currently implemented for this platform` even though the reporter could use load in Mongosh 1.1.0; a maintainer replied that the implementation had not yet been exposed in VS Code playgrounds. This is historical evidence, not a current compatibility guarantee. (low confidence)
Playground messages from `console.log()`, `print()`, and `printjson()` appear in the VS Code Output panel. (low confidence)
Open the VS Code Settings view and search for MongoDB to configure the extension; changes save automatically. (low confidence)

VSCODE-738 requests including the format in which documents are displayed or edited in document-edit telemetry events; treat this ticket as implementation intent rather than independent proof of installed behavior. (low confidence)
The repository warns that enabling autocomplete inside snippets or string literals uses global editor settings and may affect other extensions and VS Code performance. (low confidence)
The extension documents only one active deployment connection at a time; right-click a saved connection and choose Connect to activate it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

If authentication is required, include database-user credentials in the connection string: the extension warns that an initial connection might succeed without them while data interaction remains unavailable. (low confidence)

For standard Atlas connections, allow the client’s address in the project IP access list and authenticate with a database user that has access to the desired databases. An Atlas application account is separate from a database user. (medium confidence)
The extension includes an Atlas Terraform template; typing atlas in a Terraform file inserts a starting configuration. (medium confidence)
The extension can connect to Atlas Stream Processing using a Stream Processing Workspace connection string. (medium confidence)
The documented advanced connection form does not support CSFLE In-Use Encryption or Kerberos Authentication. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
The extension includes an Atlas Terraform template for creating a cluster; this is an extension feature, with provider configuration outside this concept’s scope. (medium confidence)

The legacy participant documentation lists three specialized commands: `/query` for query generation, `/schema` for collection schema information, and `/docs` for documentation links. (low confidence)

The legacy workflow let users run generated queries directly or open them in a playground; a separate Export Code to Playground action converted selected application queries into MongoDB shell syntax. (medium confidence)
The v1.18.0 release notes list participant deprecation. The linked merged PR states that it removes the @MongoDB chat participant and leaves MCP as the only AI integration. (high confidence)
MongoDB’s participant-specific AI usage documentation warns that generative AI may give inaccurate responses. (low confidence)

The documentation and release artifacts differ in scope: the overview still describes an included participant, while the v1.18.0 removal PR and release notes establish its deprecation/removal. Treat the command instructions as legacy guidance. (high confidence)

Historically, the MongoDB participant augmented GitHub Copilot Chat with MongoDB domain knowledge, natural-language query generation, collection schema information, and references to MongoDB documentation. (medium confidence)
The historical documentation demonstrates invoking @MongoDB /query to generate an aggregation pipeline and then adding another stage through a follow-up prompt. (low confidence)

The historical Export Code to Playground feature requires enabling the MongoDB Copilot extension. Selecting application query code and choosing MongoDB Copilot Extension > Export Code to Playground opens the selection in a new playground using MongoDB shell syntax. (low confidence)

Microsoft's June 24, 2024 announcement described the MongoDB chat participant as a private preview requiring signup; this is historical launch status, not evidence of present availability. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-06-24)
The Play button runs the playground against the active deployment. Selecting lines enables execution of just that portion for focused testing and troubleshooting. (low confidence)

Within standalone mongosh, `load()` executes a JavaScript file. It accepts relative or absolute paths, but it does not search for a script outside the current working directory or the specified path. (low confidence)
For portable mongosh scripts, use `db.getSiblingDB()` and supply connection details on the command line, so changing the host or port does not require editing the script. (low confidence)
MongoDB Playgrounds are JavaScript environments for prototyping queries, aggregations, and MongoDB commands with syntax highlighting. (high confidence)
A playground runs against the deployment in the active connection. (low confidence)
Selecting one or more playground lines exposes Run Selected Lines from Playground, which executes only that selection for testing or troubleshooting. (low confidence)
Playgrounds can perform create, read, update, and delete operations on collection documents using MongoDB CRUD operators and shell methods. (low confidence)
Playgrounds can reuse code through `require()` from native Node modules, external npm modules, or local JavaScript files. (medium confidence)
The local-code tutorial exports a validation function with `module.exports` and imports it in a playground with `require('/path/to/validate.js')`; the path must match the local file. (low confidence)
The playground documentation explicitly identifies `show users` as an unsupported shell command for which the editor suggests alternatives. (low confidence)

MongoDB documents Send Telemetry as enabled by default and describes its collection as anonymous diagnostic and usage telemetry. Its repository documents setting `mdb.sendTelemetry` to `false` to opt out. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Do not assume the editor telemetry switch disables every extension: Microsoft warns that extensions may collect their own usage data outside `telemetry.telemetryLevel`; MongoDB documents its own `mdb.sendTelemetry` opt-out. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04)
MongoDB documents opening extension logs through the Command Palette, running Developer: Open Log..., and selecting MongoDB Extension. (low confidence)

The logging documentation illustrates telemetry events containing an `anonymousId`, an event name and properties such as `extension_version` and `device_id`; this example is not an exhaustive inventory of collected data. (low confidence)

The settings reference exposes MongoDB language-server tracing through `mongodbLanguageServer.trace.server`, including `format` and `verbosity`; inspect output by selecting MongoDB Language Server in the Output view. (low confidence)
